title: Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

access.edition_or_version: First published 1751 as 'An Elegy Wrote in a Country Church Yard'; public-domain text (Project Gutenberg, Wikisource)

tone_mechanisms_observed: present-tense mortality meditation (the curfew, the fading landscape)
ubi sunt / vanished-labor imagery: hearth, harvest, children no longer returning
plain, largely monosyllabic diction holding strong feeling at a distance
synecdoche and epitaph: the nameless dead as 'rude forefathers'
withheld consolation: the poem closes on the speaker's own anticipated grave rather than a resolved lesson
mechanics.emotional_progression: Evening stillness -> elegiac enumeration of the unremembered dead -> meditation on thwarted potential -> turn toward the speaker's own mortality.
mechanics.point_of_view: First-person meditative observer moving among graves, widening to generalized reflection.
mechanics.rhythm_and_cadence: Iambic pentameter quatrains (ABAB) with a slow, falling cadence; heavy caesurae slow the line to a walking pace.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Tender but restrained: the speaker mourns strangers at a slight remove, then draws close to his own end.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Graveyard mode; personification of evening and death; apostrophe to abstractions (Ambition, Grandeur); emblematic rather than confessional.
mechanics.copyright_note: Public domain. Described by technique only; no passage reproduced.
